Bhante, in 'web books meditations13 section0004 html 65251b' (web books meditations13 section0004 html 65251b), what is the core doctrinal teaching regarding 'So we can’t blame our suffering'?

In this section from *web books meditations13 section0004 html 65251b*, the master explains: *"So we can’t blame our suffering on some being in charge of the universe."*. From the perspective of the Four Noble Truths, suffering arises whenever the mind grasps at impermanent phenomena (*anicca*) as a reliable self (*atta*). By establishing clear comprehension (*sampajañña*) and seeing conditioned events as empty of inherent ownership, craving (*taṇhā*) is unhooked. It is like grasping a poisonous cobra by the tail: tempting and sleek from afar, but deadly the moment you grasp it. Release the tail and live in safety. Anchor your understanding in direct seeing rather than speculative theory.

When you sit on the cushion, do not wage war against wandering thoughts. When thoughts arise, notice the space around them rather than following the story. It is like still, flowing water (nam lai rin): awareness flows smoothly perceiving sights and sounds, while the heart inside remains utterly motionless. Rest the mind gently in the rhythm of each natural in-and-out breath.
